claim: CVE-2014-1266 description: SSLVerifySignedServerKeyExchange 'does not check the signature in a TLS Server Key Exchange message, which allows man-in-the-middle attackers to spoof SSL servers by (1) using an arbitrary private key for the signing step or (2) omitting the signing step'
Langley's post of 22 Feb 2014 quoted the code from Apple's published source and said 'the signature verification will never fail'
Lines 623-633 of sslKeyExchange.c at Security-55471 read as quoted (two consecutive 'goto fail;' at 630-631)
The fail: label (lines 647-650) frees two buffers and returns err
Security-55471.14 differs from Security-55471 in this file by exactly one deleted line, line 631
The function checks the signature on the ServerKeyExchange message, used by DHE and ECDHE suites to carry the ephemeral key
A server could send a correct certificate chain and sign the handshake with the wrong key, or not sign it at all
source: Langley 22 Feb 2014 para 5; CVE-2014-1266 '(1) using an arbitrary private key ... or (2) omitting the signing step'
